book.title: A Field Guide to the Meridian Archipelago
book.subtitle: Twelve Islands, Their Charters, Their Landmarks and Their Kitchens
book.author: Compiled for the Assembly at Ashgate Quay

questions.question: Who settled Kestrel Cove?
evidence: Kestrel Cove was settled by Aurelia Halvard, who came ashore with a single crew, a borrowed sloop and a chart drawn on the back of a tide table.

questions.question: How many residents does Kestrel Cove have?
evidence: The last count recorded 412 residents on Kestrel Cove, a figure that has held steady for two generations.

questions.question: What dish is Kestrel Cove known for?
evidence: The dish that belongs to Kestrel Cove is salt-baked murren, which is finished with bladderwrack butter and served in shallow bowls.

questions.question: What festival does Kestrel Cove keep, and in which month?
evidence: the Lantern Vigil is held on Kestrel Cove every October and closes the working year for three days together.

questions.question: In what year was Thornbury Reach chartered?
evidence: Formal settlement of Thornbury Reach dates from 1701, the year the assembly at Ashgate Quay entered it in the register.

questions.question: What is the tallest structure on Thornbury Reach, and how tall is it?
evidence: The tallest structure on Thornbury Reach is the Widdershin Bridge, which stands 21 metres from its base to its cap.

questions.question: How far is Thornbury Reach from Ashgate Quay?
evidence: The crossing from Ashgate Quay to Thornbury Reach is 27 nautical miles, and the mail boat makes it twice a week.

questions.question: What does Thornbury Reach export?
evidence: Thornbury Reach trades chiefly in oyster lime, which the mainland buys faster than the island can make it.

questions.question: How many residents does Grennet Point have?
evidence: There are 940 residents on Grennet Point, and the census taker still calls at every household in person.

questions.question: What dish is Grennet Point known for?
evidence: No meal on Grennet Point is complete without charred lamb with rye; it is the juniper ash that separates it from every mainland version.

questions.question: What festival does Grennet Point keep, and in which month?
evidence: the Longlight Fair falls in May, and the boats of Grennet Point stay tied up for the whole of it.

questions.question: Who settled Grennet Point?
evidence: Islanders still name Maren Sarrowbeck as the founder of Grennet Point, although the title was never formally granted by the assembly.

questions.question: What is the tallest structure on Sable Ledge, and how tall is it?
evidence: the Drowned Chapel rises 12 metres above the shingle of Sable Ledge and is visible from every anchorage on the eastern shore.

questions.question: How far is Sable Ledge from Ashgate Quay?
evidence: Sable Ledge lies 41 nautical miles from Ashgate Quay, a passage of half a day in fair weather.

questions.question: What does Sable Ledge export?
evidence: The one cargo that leaves Sable Ledge in quantity is dyed wool, shipped out in flat crates.

questions.question: In what year was Sable Ledge chartered?
evidence: The charter of Sable Ledge was signed in 1742, and the original document still hangs in the meeting hall.

questions.question: What dish is Amberlyn Skerry known for?
evidence: Visitors to Amberlyn Skerry are given honeyed skerry pie, made with wild rosemary curd, before they are asked a single question.

questions.question: What festival does Amberlyn Skerry keep, and in which month?
evidence: Each August the households of Amberlyn Skerry keep the Amber Procession, an occasion from which nobody is excused.

questions.question: Who settled Amberlyn Skerry?
evidence: The first permanent household on Amberlyn Skerry belonged to Jonas Penlow, a boatwright who refused three separate offers to return to the mainland.

questions.question: How many residents does Amberlyn Skerry have?
evidence: Amberlyn Skerry has 733 residents, nearly all of them living within a quarter of an hour's walk of the water.

questions.question: How far is Quillon Bank from Ashgate Quay?
evidence: Reckoned from Ashgate Quay, Quillon Bank is 5 nautical miles out, a figure the pilots round up in winter.

questions.question: What does Quillon Bank export?
evidence: Nothing leaves Quillon Bank in greater volume than printed almanacs, and nothing has done for a century.

questions.question: In what year was Quillon Bank chartered?
evidence: By 1719 the survey office had accepted Quillon Bank as a chartered settlement, with its boundaries marked in cut stone.

questions.question: What is the tallest structure on Quillon Bank, and how tall is it?
evidence: the Quillon Waterworks, 18 metres tall, was raised on Quillon Bank by public subscription and has never once been altered.

questions.question: What festival does Merrowick Holt keep, and in which month?
evidence: the Rookery Count is held on Merrowick Holt every September and closes the working year for three days together.

questions.question: Who settled Merrowick Holt?
evidence: Merrowick Holt was settled by Edda Gullick, who came ashore with a single crew, a borrowed sloop and a chart drawn on the back of a tide table.

questions.question: How many residents does Merrowick Holt have?
evidence: The last count recorded 349 residents on Merrowick Holt, a figure that has held steady for two generations.

questions.question: What dish is Merrowick Holt known for?
evidence: The dish that belongs to Merrowick Holt is nettle-wrapped mackerel, which is finished with pine vinegar and served in shallow bowls.

questions.question: What does Varden Spit export?
evidence: Varden Spit trades chiefly in signal flags, which the mainland buys faster than the island can make it.

questions.question: In what year was Varden Spit chartered?
evidence: Formal settlement of Varden Spit dates from 1766, the year the assembly at Ashgate Quay entered it in the register.

questions.question: What is the tallest structure on Varden Spit, and how tall is it?
evidence: The tallest structure on Varden Spit is the Spit Semaphore, which stands 26 metres from its base to its cap.

questions.question: How far is Varden Spit from Ashgate Quay?
evidence: The crossing from Ashgate Quay to Varden Spit is 12 nautical miles, and the mail boat makes it twice a week.

questions.question: Who settled Ostrel Bight?
evidence: Islanders still name Sinnet Velmar as the founder of Ostrel Bight, although the title was never formally granted by the assembly.

questions.question: How many residents does Ostrel Bight have?
evidence: There are 214 residents on Ostrel Bight, and the census taker still calls at every household in person.

questions.question: What dish is Ostrel Bight known for?
evidence: No meal on Ostrel Bight is complete without bight chowder; it is the dried lovage that separates it from every mainland version.

questions.question: What festival does Ostrel Bight keep, and in which month?
evidence: the Cistern Blessing falls in March, and the boats of Ostrel Bight stay tied up for the whole of it.

questions.question: In what year was Falgrove Key chartered?
evidence: The charter of Falgrove Key was signed in 1698, and the original document still hangs in the meeting hall.

questions.question: What is the tallest structure on Falgrove Key, and how tall is it?
evidence: the Falgrove Ovens rises 38 metres above the shingle of Falgrove Key and is visible from every anchorage on the eastern shore.

questions.question: How far is Falgrove Key from Ashgate Quay?
evidence: Falgrove Key lies 16 nautical miles from Ashgate Quay, a passage of half a day in fair weather.

questions.question: What does Falgrove Key export?
evidence: The one cargo that leaves Falgrove Key in quantity is fired brick, shipped out in flat crates.

questions.question: How many residents does Brindlewick Sound have?
evidence: Brindlewick Sound has 902 residents, nearly all of them living within a quarter of an hour's walk of the water.

questions.question: What dish is Brindlewick Sound known for?
evidence: Visitors to Brindlewick Sound are given sound-cured herring, made with black mustard, before they are asked a single question.

questions.question: What festival does Brindlewick Sound keep, and in which month?
evidence: Each July the households of Brindlewick Sound keep the Water Reckoning, an occasion from which nobody is excused.

questions.question: Who settled Brindlewick Sound?
evidence: The first permanent household on Brindlewick Sound belonged to Wren Ryvold, a boatwright who refused three separate offers to return to the mainland.

questions.question: What is the tallest structure on Cardrenn Strand, and how tall is it?
evidence: the Strand Beacon, 15 metres tall, was raised on Cardrenn Strand by public subscription and has never once been altered.

questions.question: How far is Cardrenn Strand from Ashgate Quay?
evidence: Reckoned from Ashgate Quay, Cardrenn Strand is 52 nautical miles out, a figure the pilots round up in winter.

questions.question: What does Cardrenn Strand export?
evidence: Nothing leaves Cardrenn Strand in greater volume than sea salt, and nothing has done for a century.

questions.question: In what year was Cardrenn Strand chartered?
evidence: By 1754 the survey office had accepted Cardrenn Strand as a chartered settlement, with its boundaries marked in cut stone.

questions.question: Which was chartered earlier, Kestrel Cove or Thornbury Reach?
evidence: The charter of Kestrel Cove was signed in 1673, and the original document still hangs in the meeting hall.
Formal settlement of Thornbury Reach dates from 1701, the year the assembly at Ashgate Quay entered it in the register.

questions.question: Whose landmark is taller, the one on Merrowick Holt or the one on Brindlewick Sound?

The tallest structure on Brindlewick Sound is the Sound Aqueduct, which stands 63 metres from its base to its cap.
